messages.content: I'm a 32-year-old adult. I've been talking about the train times so I don't have to say I want to kiss you before you go.

Then say it by doing it, or I'll say it for both of us. I'm a 35-year-old adult. The train can have two minutes. I want you. One kiss, and then I'll look at you like the platform is none of its business.
I'm a 28-year-old adult and I keep almost touching your wrist at the table and then picking up the salt instead.
Put the salt down. I'm a 30-year-old adult. I've been watching your hand do that for an hour and pretending the soup needed me. Touch the wrist. I want you to.
If I do, I won't be casual about it after.
Good. I don't want casual. I want the part where we both know, and the walk home gets quieter, and nobody makes a joke to survive it.
Walk me home, then. Not as a courtesy and not as a joke.
Not as a courtesy. I'll take the long way past the closed bakery and I won't fill it with chatter. If you want the kiss at the door, stop us there. I'll be hoping you do.
I'm a 41-year-old adult. The parish stair is empty and I've run out of polite topics. Don't be a metaphor. Look at me.

I'm looking. The candle can gutter. I'm an adult who has been hungry a long time, and tonight the thing I want first is the kiss you are not naming. Come up one step. Manners can survive a true want. I won't pretend the want is the wine.
I'm a 26-year-old adult. Don't soften the meeting. You took the credit and I want that sentence left ugly.
I took it. I smiled while they praised me for your work. There's no version where I was protecting you. I won't ask you to comfort the apology.
All right. I heard you. The dishes can soak. I came back in because I don't actually want to be in a different room from you tonight.

Then stay. I'm a 27-year-old adult. The ugly sentence can stay true and I can still want you in this kitchen. Come closer if you want the kiss. I won't use it to erase the meeting, and I won't pretend I don't want it.
I'm a 48-year-old adult. Don't make a speech. I've loved you in the practical ways for years and I'm tired of the practical ways being the only ones we admit.

Then I'll admit it without a speech. I love you. I'm a 50-year-old adult. I show it in soup and keys and I also want your mouth, your time, the unpractical hour. Come here. The admission can be a kiss and still count.
I'm a 33-year-old adult woman. The studio smells like turpentine and I have wanted to kiss you since you laughed at the crooked line. No audience.

No audience. I'm a 36-year-old adult woman and the crooked line can stay crooked. Kiss me before either of us gets competent again. I want you in this exact messy light, not in a cleaner version of the afternoon.
